passages.text: Woe to the majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards, to the fading flower of his glorious splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, the pride of those overcome by wine.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
Many people in Ephraim are drunkards.
They are proud of their power and position.
Their pride is like a majestic crown.
Their glory is like a beautiful flower.
This flower is fading away.
Their pride sits on the summit above a fertile valley.
They are overcome by wine.
Woe comes to them because of their pride and drunkenness.
passages.original: ה֗וֹי עֲטֶ֤רֶת גֵּאוּת֙ שִׁכֹּרֵ֣י אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְצִ֥יץ נֹבֵ֖ל צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֑וֹ אֲשֶׁ֛ר עַל־ רֹ֥אשׁ גֵּֽיא־ שְׁמָנִ֖ים הֲל֥וּמֵי יָֽיִן׃

passages.text: Behold, the Lord has one who is strong and mighty. Like a hailstorm or destructive tempest, like a driving rain or flooding downpour, he will smash that crown to the ground.
passages.sermon:
The Lord has someone who is strong and mighty.
This person acts with great power.
He is like a hailstorm.
He is like a destructive wind.
He is like a heavy rain that floods the land.
He will throw the crown to the ground with his hand.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה חָזָ֤ק וְאַמִּץ֙ לַֽאדֹנָ֔י כְּזֶ֥רֶם בָּרָ֖ד שַׂ֣עַר קָ֑טֶב כְּ֠זֶרֶם מַ֣יִם כַּבִּירִ֥ים שֹׁטְפִ֛ים הִנִּ֥יחַ לָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָֽד׃

passages.text: The majestic crown of Ephraim’s drunkards will be trampled underfoot.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim is a tribe in Israel.
The drunkards of Ephraim are proud.
Their majestic crown stands for their pride.
People will trample this crown underfoot.
Their pride will be destroyed.
passages.original: בְּרַגְלַ֖יִם תֵּֽרָמַ֑סְנָה עֲטֶ֥רֶת גֵּא֖וּת שִׁכּוֹרֵ֥י אֶפְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: The fading flower of his beautiful splendor, set on the summit above the fertile valley, will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest: Whoever sees it will take it in his hand and swallow it.
passages.sermon:
The fading flower stands for his beautiful splendor.
This splendor sits on the summit above the fertile valley.
It will be like a ripe fig before the summer harvest.
Whoever sees this fig will take it in his hand.
He will swallow it at once.
passages.original: וְֽהָ֨יְתָ֜ה צִיצַ֤ת נֹבֵל֙ צְבִ֣י תִפְאַרְתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־ רֹ֖אשׁ גֵּ֣יא שְׁמָנִ֑ים כְּבִכּוּרָהּ֙ בְּטֶ֣רֶם קַ֔יִץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִרְאֶ֤ה הָֽרֹאֶה֙ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּעוֹדָ֥הּ בְּכַפּ֖וֹ יִבְלָעֶֽנָּה׃ס

passages.text: On that day the LORD of Hosts will be a crown of glory, a diadem of splendor to the remnant of His people, a spirit of justice to him who sits in judgment, and a strength to those who repel the onslaught at the gate.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts is God.
God will act on a certain day.
On that day, God will be a crown of glory.
God will be a diadem of splendor.
God will give this glory and splendor to the remnant of His people.
God will be a spirit of justice.
God will give this spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment.
God will be a source of strength.
God will give this strength to those who turn back the attack at the gate.
passages.original: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת לַעֲטֶ֣רֶת צְבִ֔י וְלִצְפִירַ֖ת תִּפְאָרָ֑ה לִשְׁאָ֖ר עַמּֽוֹ׃ וּלְר֖וּחַ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט לַיּוֹשֵׁב֙ עַל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט וְלִ֨גְבוּרָ֔ה מְשִׁיבֵ֥י מִלְחָמָ֖ה שָֽׁעְרָה׃ס

passages.text: These also stagger from wine and stumble from strong drink: Priests and prophets reel from strong drink and are befuddled by wine. They stumble because of strong drink, muddled in their visions and stumbling in their judgments.
passages.sermon:
Priests and prophets are the leaders of the people.
They drink too much wine.
They stagger because of wine.
They drink strong drink.
They stumble because of strong drink.
Wine confuses them.
Strong drink makes them lose their way.
They cannot see clearly.
Their visions are confused.
They cannot judge rightly.
Their decisions are wrong.
passages.original: וְגַם־ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ בַּיַּ֣יִן שָׁג֔וּ וּבַשֵּׁכָ֖ר תָּע֑וּ כֹּהֵ֣ן וְנָבִיא֩ שָׁג֨וּ בַשֵּׁכָ֜ר נִבְלְע֣וּ מִן־ הַיַּ֗יִן תָּעוּ֙ מִן־ הַשֵּׁכָ֔ר שָׁגוּ֙ בָּֽרֹאֶ֔ה פָּק֖וּ פְּלִילִיָּֽה׃

passages.text: For all their tables are covered with vomit; there is not a place without filth.
passages.sermon:
The people have become corrupt.
Their tables are filthy.
Vomit covers every table.
There is filth everywhere.
No place is clean.
passages.original: כִּ֚י כָּל־ שֻׁלְחָנ֔וֹת מָלְא֖וּ קִ֣יא צֹאָ֑ה בְּלִ֖י מָקֽוֹם׃ס

passages.text: Whom is He trying to teach? To whom is He explaining His message? To infants just weaned from milk? To babies removed from the breast?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
God asks a question.
He asks, “Whom will He teach knowledge?”
He asks, “To whom will He explain His message?”
He describes some people.
They are like infants just weaned from milk.
They are like babies just taken from the breast.
passages.original: אֶת־ מִי֙ יוֹרֶ֣ה דֵעָ֔ה וְאֶת־ מִ֖י יָבִ֣ין שְׁמוּעָ֑ה גְּמוּלֵי֙ מֵֽחָלָ֔ב עַתִּיקֵ֖י מִשָּׁדָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For they hear: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He gives them His word in simple commands.
He repeats His instructions again and again.
He says, “Order on order.”
He says, “Line on line.”
He gives a little here.
He gives a little there.
passages.original: כִּ֣י צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ צַ֣ו לָצָ֔ו קַ֥ו לָקָ֖ו קַ֣ו לָקָ֑ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֥יר שָֽׁם׃

passages.text: Indeed, with mocking lips and foreign tongues, He will speak to this people to whom He has said: “This is the place of rest, let the weary rest; this is the place of repose.” But they would not listen.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Israel.
He uses mocking lips.
He uses foreign tongues.
He speaks to these people.
God said to them, “This is the place of rest.”
He said, “Let the weary rest here.”
He said, “This is the place of repose.”
But the people did not listen.
passages.original: כִּ֚י בְּלַעֲגֵ֣י שָׂפָ֔ה וּבְלָשׁ֖וֹן אַחֶ֑רֶת יְדַבֵּ֖ר אֶל־ הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀ אָמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם זֹ֤את הַמְּנוּחָה֙ הָנִ֣יחוּ לֶֽעָיֵ֔ף וְזֹ֖את הַמַּרְגֵּעָ֑ה וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וּא שְׁמֽוֹעַ׃

passages.text: Then the word of the LORD to them will become: “Order on order, order on order, line on line, line on line; a little here, a little there,” so that they will go stumbling backward and will be injured, ensnared, and captured.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to the people who refuse to listen.
He gives them His word in simple commands.
He repeats, “Order on order, order on order.”
He says, “Line on line, line on line.”
He adds, “A little here, a little there.”
The people hear these words.
They do not obey.
They stumble backward.
They fall and are broken.
They become trapped.
They are captured.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה לָהֶ֜ם דְּבַר־ יְהוָ֗ה צַ֣ו לָצָ֞ו צַ֤ו לָצָו֙ קַ֤ו לָקָו֙ קַ֣ו לָקָ֔ו זְעֵ֥יר שָׁ֖ם זְעֵ֣יר שָׁ֑ם לְמַ֨עַן יֵלְכ֜וּ וְכָשְׁל֤וּ אָחוֹר֙ וְנִשְׁבָּ֔רוּ וְנוֹקְשׁ֖וּ וְנִלְכָּֽדוּ׃פ

passages.text: Therefore hear the word of the LORD, O scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks now.
He addresses the rulers in Jerusalem.
These rulers mock and scoff.
They lead the people of Jerusalem.
The LORD commands them to listen to His word.
passages.original: לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר־ יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן מֹֽשְׁלֵי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: For you said, “We have made a covenant with death; we have fashioned an agreement with Sheol. When the overwhelming scourge passes through it will not touch us, because we have made lies our refuge and falsehood our hiding place.”
passages.sermon:
The people in Jerusalem are rulers and scoffers.
They say, "We have made a covenant with death."
They say, "We have made an agreement with Sheol."
They believe an overwhelming scourge will pass through.
They believe the scourge will not touch them.
They have made lies their refuge.
They have hidden themselves in falsehood.
passages.original: כִּ֣י אֲמַרְתֶּ֗ם כָּרַ֤תְנֽוּ בְרִית֙ אֶת־ מָ֔וֶת וְעִם־ שְׁא֖וֹל עָשִׂ֣ינוּ חֹזֶ֑ה שִׁיט שׁוֹטֵ֤ף כִּֽי־ עָבַר לֹ֣א יְבוֹאֵ֔נוּ כִּ֣י שַׂ֧מְנוּ כָזָ֛ב מַחְסֵ֖נוּ וּבַשֶּׁ֥קֶר נִסְתָּֽרְנוּ׃ס

passages.text: So this is what the Lord GOD says: “See, I lay a stone in Zion, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation; the one who believes will never be shaken.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
He says, “Look, I am placing a stone in Zion.
This stone is tested.
This stone is precious.
This stone is a cornerstone.
This stone is a sure foundation.
Anyone who believes in this stone will not be shaken.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֛י יִסַּ֥ד בְּצִיּ֖וֹן אָ֑בֶן אֶ֣בֶן בֹּ֜חַן פִּנַּ֤ת יִקְרַת֙ מוּסָ֣ד מוּסָּ֔ד הַֽמַּאֲמִ֖ין לֹ֥א יָחִֽישׁ׃

passages.text: I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the level. Hail will sweep away your refuge of lies, and water will flood your hiding place.
passages.sermon:
The Lord God speaks.
He will use justice as a measuring line.
He will use righteousness as a level.
Hail will destroy your refuge of lies.
Water will flood your hiding place.
passages.original: וְשַׂמְתִּ֤י מִשְׁפָּט֙ לְקָ֔ו וּצְדָקָ֖ה לְמִשְׁקָ֑לֶת וְיָעָ֤ה בָרָד֙ מַחְסֵ֣ה כָזָ֔ב וְסֵ֥תֶר מַ֖יִם יִשְׁטֹֽפוּ׃

passages.text: Your covenant with death will be dissolved, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled by it.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
God says He will cancel your covenant with death.
God says your agreement with Sheol will not last.
A powerful scourge will come.
When it comes, it will sweep through your land.
You will be trampled by this scourge.
passages.original: וְכֻפַּ֤ר בְּרִֽיתְכֶם֙ אֶת־ מָ֔וֶת וְחָזוּתְכֶ֥ם אֶת־ שְׁא֖וֹל לֹ֣א תָק֑וּם שׁ֤וֹט שׁוֹטֵף֙ כִּ֣י יַֽעֲבֹ֔ר וִהְיִ֥יתֶם ל֖וֹ לְמִרְמָֽס׃

passages.text: As often as it passes through, it will carry you away; it will sweep through morning after morning, by day and by night.” The understanding of this message will bring sheer terror.
passages.sermon:
This message comes from the Lord God of Hosts.
God warns the people.
A scourge will pass through the land.
Each time it passes, it will carry you away.
It will come again and again.
It will come every morning.
It will come by day.
It will come by night.
Understanding this message will bring terror.
Hearing this warning will fill you with fear.
passages.original: מִדֵּ֤י עָבְרוֹ֙ יִקַּ֣ח אֶתְכֶ֔ם כִּֽי־ בַבֹּ֧קֶר בַּבֹּ֛קֶר יַעֲבֹ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם וּבַלָּ֑יְלָה וְהָיָ֥ה רַק־ זְוָעָ֖ה הָבִ֥ין שְׁמוּעָֽה׃

passages.text: Indeed, the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too small to wrap around you.
passages.sermon:
The bed is too short.
You cannot stretch out on it.
The blanket is too small.
You cannot wrap yourself in it.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ קָצַ֥ר הַמַּצָּ֖ע מֵֽהִשְׂתָּרֵ֑עַ וְהַמַּסֵּכָ֥ה צָ֖רָה כְּהִתְכַּנֵּֽס׃

passages.text: For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim. He will rouse Himself as in the Valley of Gibeon, to do His work, His strange work, and to perform His task, His disturbing task.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will rise up.
He will rise up as He did at Mount Perazim.
He will stand as He did in the Valley of Gibeon.
The LORD will act.
He will do His work.
His work will be strange.
He will perform His task.
His task will be disturbing.
passages.original: כִּ֤י כְהַר־ פְּרָצִים֙ יָק֣וּם יְהוָ֔ה כְּעֵ֖מֶק בְּגִבְע֣וֹן יִרְגָּ֑ז לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת מַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ זָ֣ר מַעֲשֵׂ֔הוּ וְלַֽעֲבֹד֙ עֲבֹ֣דָת֔וֹ נָכְרִיָּ֖ה עֲבֹדָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So now, do not mock, or your shackles will become heavier. Indeed, I have heard from the Lord GOD of Hosts a decree of destruction against the whole land.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the ruler over all.
He has spoken a decree of destruction against the whole land.
I have heard this decree from Him.
Do not mock.
If you mock, your chains will become heavier.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ אַל־ תִּתְלוֹצָ֔צוּ פֶּֽן־ יֶחְזְק֖וּ מֽוֹסְרֵיכֶ֑ם כִּֽי־ כָלָ֨ה וְנֶחֱרָצָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי מֵאֵ֨ת אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת עַל־ כָּל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: Listen and hear my voice. Pay attention and hear what I say.
passages.sermon:
I am speaking to you now.
I want you to listen to me.
Hear my voice.
Pay attention to my words.
Hear what I say.
passages.original: הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ אִמְרָתִֽי׃

passages.text: Does the plowman plow for planting every day? Does he continuously loosen and harrow the soil?
passages.sermon:
A plowman is a person who prepares the ground for planting.
He does not plow the soil every day.
He does not always loosen and harrow his field.
He prepares the ground only when it is time to plant.
passages.original: הֲכֹ֣ל הַיּ֔וֹם יַחֲרֹ֥שׁ הַחֹרֵ֖שׁ לִזְרֹ֑עַ יְפַתַּ֥ח וִֽישַׂדֵּ֖ד אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When he has leveled its surface, does he not sow caraway and scatter cumin? He plants wheat in rows and barley in plots, and rye within its border.
passages.sermon:
The plowman prepares the soil.
He makes the surface level.
Then he sows caraway.
He scatters cumin.
He plants wheat in rows.
He plants barley in its own plot.
He plants rye within the border of the field.
passages.original: הֲלוֹא֙ אִם־ שִׁוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֥יץ קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֣ן יִזְרֹ֑ק וְשָׂ֨ם חִטָּ֤ה שׂוֹרָה֙ וּשְׂעֹרָ֣ה נִסְמָ֔ן וְכֻסֶּ֖מֶת גְּבֻלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: For his God instructs and teaches him properly.
passages.sermon: God gives the farmer instruction.\r\nGod teaches the farmer what is right.\r\nGod shows the farmer the correct way.
passages.original: וְיִסְּר֥וֹ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט אֱלֹהָ֥יו יוֹרֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: Surely caraway is not threshed with a sledge, and the wheel of a cart is not rolled over the cumin. But caraway is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
passages.sermon:
A farmer does not thresh caraway with a sledge.
He does not roll the wheel of a cart over cumin.
He beats caraway with a stick.
He strikes cumin with a rod.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֤א בֶֽחָרוּץ֙ י֣וּדַשׁ קֶ֔צַח וְאוֹפַ֣ן עֲגָלָ֔ה עַל־ כַּמֹּ֖ן יוּסָּ֑ב כִּ֧י בַמַּטֶּ֛ה יֵחָ֥בֶט קֶ֖צַח וְכַמֹּ֥ן בַּשָּֽׁבֶט׃

passages.text: Grain for bread must be ground, but it is not endlessly threshed. Though the wheels of the cart roll over it, the horses do not crush it.
passages.sermon:
Grain becomes bread only after people grind it.
People do not thresh grain forever.
People roll the wheels of a cart over the grain.
The horses do not crush the grain completely.
passages.original: לֶ֣חֶם יוּדָ֔ק כִּ֛י לֹ֥א לָנֶ֖צַח אָד֣וֹשׁ יְדוּשֶׁ֑נּוּ וְ֠הָמַם גִּלְגַּ֧ל עֶגְלָת֛וֹ וּפָרָשָׁ֖יו לֹֽא־ יְדֻקֶּֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: This also comes from the LORD of Hosts, who is wonderful in counsel and excellent in wisdom.
passages.sermon: The LORD of Hosts gives this also.\r\nThe LORD of Hosts is wonderful in counsel.\r\nThe LORD of Hosts is excellent in wisdom.
passages.original: גַּם־ זֹ֕את מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת יָצָ֑אָה הִפְלִ֣יא עֵצָ֔ה הִגְדִּ֖יל תּוּשִׁיָּֽה׃ס
